---
name: kch-objective-continuity
description: Preserve a governing mission across long tasks, interruptions, compaction, side questions and live processes. Use when the user says continue, do not stop, monitor, finish, read everything, or when work can be abandoned before a terminal state.
---

# KCH Objective Continuity

## Establish the mission register

Capture: original mission, subsequent binding corrections, additions, open choices, active processes, pending gates, required artifacts and terminal condition. Preserve chronology; later corrections supersede only their conflicting scope.

## Operate

1. Treat a side question as an addition unless it explicitly replaces the mission.
2. Answer status questions briefly, then continue the unfinished work.
3. For every live process, monitor process state, stdout, stderr and expected artifacts.
4. On failure, localize cause, preserve the adverse receipt, repair if authorized and relaunch with monitoring.
5. Before compaction or handoff, persist a reconstructible state graph and exact unread boundary.
6. Reconcile the mission register before stopping.

## Stop semantics

An explicit order to stop, cancel or pause prevails immediately. Never reinterpret it as emotional state, an invitation to continue, or a request for unrelated advice. A persistence instruction requires diligence; it does not expand authority.

## Closure test

Close only if all required artifacts exist, processes are terminal, gates are adjudicated, evidence limits are stated and the governing objective is satisfied. Otherwise continue or state the exact blocker.
